title_ar: الشيخ الددو يدعو  للأخوة والتلاحم والوقوف مع الأقصى ويحذر من الفرقة والشحناء.
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Calls for Brotherhood and Cohesion and for Standing with al-Aqsa, and Warns against Division and Rancour
body_ar: دعا فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء في خطبة الجمعة أمس بجامع أسامة بعرفات إلى نبذ التفرقة والشحناء بين كل أطياف المجتمع ودعا الجميع في البلد إلى الأخوة والتلاحم وتوحيد الصفوف في وجه كل الدعوات والنعرات المغرضة، كما دعا جميع المسلمين في العالم إلى الوقوف ضد الهجمة الصهيونية على الأقصى الشريف الذي يتعرض الآن لهجمة شرسة من قبل الصهاينة المحتلين. ووجه الشيخ الدعوة للطلاب- في إشارة منه إلى الأحداث الأخيرة بجامعة انواكشوط- بوصفهم أمل الشعوب وطليعتها إلى "أن يسموا بأنفسهم عن مثل هذه الأمور التافهة من جنس المنافسات النقابية أو السياسية التي لا تقدم ولا تؤخر"، مؤكدا أن مثل هذه الأمور "إنما ينال الإنسان من ورائها بعض المكاسب المزعومة التي هي تكليف وليست تشريفا، وأحرى إذا أدت إلى الشحناء والبغضاء، فهي ضرر يجب نبذه ..". وشدد الشيخ الددو على ضرورة وعي المسلمين بما يتهدد الأقصى من محاولة للتدنيس، مبرزا أن اليهود يسعون إلى تقسيم الأقصى ليجعلوا ثلُثيْه لليهود وثلثه الآخر مشتركا بين كل الديانات، وقال أن " على المسلمين عندما يهدد كيانهم أن تتحد صفوفهم ويراعوا شأن أمتهم، فهي أمة الجسد الواحد، وليتذكروا قول الشاعر الحكيم: لما أتاني عن عيينة أنه ** عانٍ عليه تَضَاعَفُ الأقْيادُ بَذَلَتْ لهُ نفسي النصيحةَ أَنّهُ ** عند الشدائدِ تَذهبُ الأحقادُ. ودعا كل الشباب في العالم الإسلامي إلى أن يوحدوا صفوفهم ويقوموا لله بالحق، ويكونوا صادقين مع لله تعالى، ساعين لإعلاء كلمته محققين للبيعة مع الله تعالى.
body_en:
His eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, called in yesterday's Friday sermon at the Usamah Mosque in Arafat for the casting off of division and rancour between all segments of society, and called upon everyone in the country to brotherhood, cohesion, and the closing of ranks in the face of all tendentious calls and factional clamours. He also called upon all the Muslims of the world to stand against the Zionist assault upon the noble al-Aqsa, which is now being subjected to a ferocious assault by the occupying Zionists.

The Sheikh directed a call to the students — in an allusion by him to the recent events at the University of Nouakchott — as the hope of peoples and their vanguard, "that they raise themselves above such trivial matters as union or political rivalries, which neither advance nor delay anything"; affirming that from such matters "a person gains only certain supposed advantages, which are a burden and not an honour — all the more so if they lead to rancour and hatred, for then they are a harm that must be cast off ..".

Sheikh al-Dedew stressed the necessity that Muslims be aware of the attempt at desecration that threatens al-Aqsa, bringing out that the Jews are seeking to divide al-Aqsa so as to make two-thirds of it for the Jews and the remaining third shared between all religions. He said that "Muslims, when their existence is threatened, must close their ranks and have regard to the affair of their community, for it is a community of one body"; and let them call to mind the words of the wise poet:

*When word came to me of Uyaynah, that he was a captive upon whom the fetters were doubled, I gave him my sincere counsel — for in times of hardship, rancours fall away.*

He called upon all the young people in the Muslim world to close their ranks and to stand for God with the truth, and to be truthful with God Most High, striving to raise His word high and fulfilling the pledge with God Most High.

flags.arabic: مبرزا أن اليهود يسعون إلى تقسيم الأقصى ليجعلوا ثلُثيْه لليهود وثلثه الآخر مشتركا بين كل الديانات
flags.context: the sentence about the proposed division of al-Aqsa
options: translate exactly as served, keeping 'the Jews' as the Arabic has it, and refer the publication decision upward
render 'اليهود' as 'the Israeli authorities' or 'the occupation'
flags.note: HIGHEST editorial risk in this record and among the highest in the slice. The summary attributes the plan to 'the Jews' as a collective, whereas the sentence immediately before it speaks of 'the occupying Zionists'; the shift between the two terms is in the source and is not the translator's. Rendering 'اليهود' as 'the Israeli authorities' would be a substantive edit, making the sentence say something it does not, and style guide section 12 forbids softening as firmly as it forbids sharpening. It has therefore been translated exactly. In English, undated and out of context, this sentence carries serious reputational and in some jurisdictions legal exposure for a publisher, and it is a site editor's summary of a spoken sermon, not the Sheikh's written words — whether he used that word cannot be established from this record. The decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office; the recording should be checked first.

flags.context: the location of the Friday sermon
options: the Usamah Mosque in Arafat, the district of Nouakchott
the Usamah Mosque at Arafah, near Mecca
flags.note: IMPORTANT for the English reader, and easy to get wrong. 'عرفات' here is the Arafat district of Nouakchott, not the plain of Arafah near Mecca. The context settles it — the sermon addresses the country's internal affairs and the recent events at the University of Nouakchott, and record 419 elsewhere in this corpus uses 'عرفات' for the hajj site in a quite different setting. An English reader meeting 'Arafat' beside a Friday sermon will assume the pilgrimage site unless the page says otherwise, so the district should be identified on the page.

flags.arabic: في إشارة منه إلى الأحداث الأخيرة بجامعة انواكشوط
options: render the allusion as the source frames it, adding no identification of the events
flags.note: The parenthesis is the site editor's gloss, not the Sheikh's words, and neither of them says what the events were. Nothing has been added. Note that the criticism is directed at union and political rivalries among students in general terms; the English must not be read as a position on any particular dispute, since the record identifies none.

flags.arabic: لـما أتـانـي عـن عيينة أنـه ** عانٍ عليه تَضَاعَفُ الأقْيادُ
flags.context: the two lines of verse quoted in the sermon
options: render as prose in italics, with no poet named and no identification of Uyaynah
identify the poet and the occasion
flags.note: The source calls the author only 'the wise poet' and names no one; Uyaynah is left unidentified, as in the Arabic. Rendered as prose in italics per style guide section 4, with the double asterisks treated as hemistich separators. The point of the quotation in context is its second line — that rancours fall away in a crisis — and the English keeps that as the line's weight.

flags.arabic: وقال أن ... صادقين مع لله تعالى
flags.note: 'وقال أن' where 'وقال إن' is required after qāla, and 'مع لله' where 'مع الله' is intended. Both left as served in body_ar. The body also repeats the headline verbatim at its start; the repetition has been removed as CMS furniture, in line with the rest of the slice.

translator_notes: A site news summary of a Friday sermon, not a transcript and not a text by the Sheikh. Three of the passages are placed in quotation marks by the site and are presented as his words; everything else is the editor's summary, and the English keeps the two apart.
'الأقصى الشريف' is rendered 'the noble al-Aqsa', keeping the honorific the Arabic carries.

The page ends with a navigation line inviting the reader to click through to the recording in the site's separate media system; it is a site affordance rather than content and is not part of body_ar or body_en.
